issues.failure_explanation: The abstract, introduction and Section 2 assert that grade-wise training (the MGDL optimization algorithm of Section 2.1) yields vanishing approximation error. Theorem thm:main:mgdl only proves that there EXIST affine maps (chosen analytically, with each layer carrying the identity so later grades can build on it) whose residuals vanish. Nothing is shown about the residuals produced by grade-wise loss minimization; indeed a greedy grade-1 minimizer can select a block that destroys input information, after which the constructed later grades are unavailable. The paper's own conclusion concedes the learned-parameter case is open.

failure_location.quote: To the best of our knowledge, this work provides the first rigorous theoretical guarantee that grade-wise training yields provable vanishing approximation error in deep networks.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reword all such claims to state that the MGDL architecture admits a (constructive) choice of grade blocks with vanishing residuals, not that the training algorithm achieves it.
issues.overall_effect: Statements that grade-wise training is guaranteed to converge (abstract, Section 1, Section 2.1 'affirmative answer') are unsupported; only an approximation-theoretic existence result for the MGDL architecture is established.
issues.title: Prose claims a guarantee for grade-wise *training*, but only an existence/construction result is proved
issues.why_classification: The repair is a rewording but it withdraws the paper's headline promise about training; the formal results themselves are untouched.

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem thm:main:mgdl:one:op constructs maps A_1,...,A_n acting from the raw input x. In the second and later rounds of the proof of thm:main:mgdl, the new updates h_k for k>n_1 must be of the form A_k^out ∘ (ReLU∘A_k) ∘ ... ∘ (ReLU∘A_1) with A_1,...,A_{n_1} already fixed. The theorem as stated does not assert that such maps exist given an arbitrary frozen prefix; the argument implicitly needs the additional property (visible only in Figure fig:h:k) that every constructed layer passes the identity x through, so that later grades can act on x. This is not stated or proved.

issues.failure_explanation: The explicit subsequence k_j = Σ n_i yields contraction by the factor 1-ε_0 where ε_0<1/(1+2^d) is the parameter fixed when the maps in thm:main:mgdl were built. The corollary is stated for arbitrary ε∈(0,1), and the residuals R_k are fixed before ε is chosen, so the advertised explicit construction is not provided for ε≥1/(1+2^d) (nor for any ε different from ε_0). Existence of such a subsequence for general ε follows only from the purely existential fact that ‖R_k‖∞→0, contrary to the text's emphasis.

Since both $a(\bm{x})$ and $b(\bm{x})$ lie between $0$ and $(1-\varepsilon)\|g\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)}$

issues.failure_explanation: The definition of a positive ε-contraction only gives ‖g^+−Tg‖∞ ≤ (1−ε)‖g^+‖∞; it does not give the lower bound 0 ≤ g^+−Tg that the proof uses to confine a(x), b(x) to [0,(1−ε)‖g‖]. Without it, a−b can reach 2(1−ε)‖g‖. Counterexample: fix x_0, θ(g)=sign(g(x_0)) (with θ=1 if g(x_0)=0), Tg := g^+ + (1−ε)‖g^+‖∞ θ(g). Then T is a positive ε-contraction on C(Ω), but for g with ‖g^+‖=‖g^-‖=1 and g(x_0)≠0, g−Sg = −(1−ε)θ(g)·2, so ‖g−Sg‖∞ = 2(1−ε)‖g‖∞ > (1−ε)‖g‖∞ when ε<1/2. The lemma is thus false as stated; it needs the hypothesis Tg ≤ g^+ pointwise (condition C1), which does hold for the operator T_ε actually used.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Each such cutoff function can be implemented exactly by a shallow \ReLU{} network.

issues.failure_explanation: ψ is a trapezoid equal to 1 on [−1,1] and 0 outside [−r,r]. For d≥2, Ψ(x)=(1/d)Σψ(x_i) is nonzero whenever ANY coordinate satisfies |x_i|<r (e.g. d=2, x=(c_1, far): Ψ=1/2), so Γ_Q is supported on an unbounded union of slabs, not on rQ, violating the definition's requirement Γ_Q=0 outside rQ. Consequently in the proof of lem:T:positive:eps:contraction: (a) T_ε g is nonzero at points outside ∪rQ_i, including points where g<0, so 0≤T_εg≤g^+ (C1) fails; (b) the overlap bound Σ_i Γ_{Q_i}(x) ≤ 2^d from lem:bounded:overlap:scaling does not apply since the slabs of many cubes can contain x. Hence T_ε is not a positive ε-contraction as constructed, and the case analyses in thm:main:mgdl:one:op ('h_k(x)=0 for x∈Ω_2', strict L^p decrease) collapse. Moreover, a genuinely compactly supported cutoff cannot be a single-hidden-layer ReLU network in d≥2 (finite sums of ridge functions with compact support vanish), so the advertised realization of Γ_Q by one ReLU layer of 4d units per grade is impossible; an extra ReLU (e.g. σ(Σψ(x_i)−(d−1))) in a subsequent layer is required. The argument is correct only for d=1.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace Γ_Q by a true cutoff such as σ(Σ_i ψ(2(x_i−c_i)/ℓ) − (d−1)) and restructure the network so each grade's layer computes the 4d trapezoid units for the current cube plus the thresholding unit for the previous cube (width 5d+1, identity carried), adjusting indexing so each grade still outputs one cutoff (possibly weakening strict L^p decrease at the very first grade or adding a preparatory grade).
issues.overall_effect: For d≥2 the one-step contraction, the pointwise domination and strict L^p monotonicity, and hence Theorem thm:main:mgdl and its corollary, are unproved; the width-5d single-layer-per-grade realization claim is false as stated.
issues.title: Constructed cutoff Γ_Q = (1/d)Σψ(x_i) is not supported in rQ for d≥2, breaking condition C1 and the single-layer realization
issues.why_classification: The core construction must be rebuilt with an added layer/unit per cube and re-verified, but a recognizably comparable fixed-width result with the same contraction mechanism survives; no new global architecture is needed.
